_doc: This is the machine-readable half of your project's contract with the loop.
The other half is the '## SDLC Contract' section of your CLAUDE.md: rules a
script cannot check, written for the assistant to read.
Nothing here starts the loop: a person does, by typing /sdlc:next in Claude Code.
Commands run from the repository root. Leave one empty to skip that step.
The coverage and mutation commands must print their percentage as the last
Run 'sdlc doctor' after changing anything here.
_commands_doc: Checked against Taskfile.yml, which is what CI runs as './task check'.
lint, fmt and fmt_check go through ./task so they use the golangci-lint the
Taskfile pins and the gofmt of the toolchain go.mod pins, not whatever is on PATH.
test is './task test' plus -count=1: the packages Taskfile.yml names in
NO_RACE_PKGS without -race, every other with it. Both write a coverage profile
as they go, because a second run of the suite for the figure alone doubled
every landing. Raced and profiled at once, internal/shellpolicy took 26 minutes
where it takes 8 raced and 3 profiled, so it is not raced here either. The
profile is there only after a run that passed, and coverage refuses one older
than the code. npm_test is not one the loop runs by name:
it needs node on PATH, and is for a story that touches npm/.
freeze_check lints the tree and compiles every test without running one, so a
test that does not lint or build is corrected before the freeze, not after it.
test_files is the freeze's narrow run: only the packages that hold the files in
SDLC_TEST_FILES, and the npm tests when a .test.js file is among them, so a
freeze no longer runs the whole twenty-minute suite to see the new tests fail.

commands.test: plain=$(sed -n 's/^ *NO_RACE_PKGS: *//p' Taskfile.yml) && test -n "$plain" && mkdir -p .scratch && rm -f .scratch/cover.out && go list $plain > .scratch/plain.txt && go test -timeout 20m -count=1 -covermode=atomic -coverprofile=.scratch/plain.tmp $plain && go test -race -timeout 20m -count=1 -coverprofile=.scratch/raced.tmp $(go list ./... | grep -vxF -f .scratch/plain.txt) && { cat .scratch/raced.tmp && tail -n +2 .scratch/plain.tmp; } > .scratch/cover.out
commands.fmt_file: case "$FILE" in *.go) GOTOOLCHAIN="$(sed -n 's/^toolchain //p' go.mod | head -n 1)" go fmt "$FILE" >/dev/null ;; esac
commands.coverage: test -f .scratch/cover.out && test -z "$(find cmd internal test -name '*.go' -newer .scratch/cover.out | head -n 1)" || { echo 'no coverage profile for this tree: run commands.test first, which writes it' >&2; exit 1; }; go tool cover -func=.scratch/cover.out | tail -1 | grep -Eo '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+'
commands.test_files: if [ -n "${SDLC_TEST_FILES-}" ]; then r=0; p=$(grep -v '\.test\.js$' "$SDLC_TEST_FILES" | sed -e 's#^#./#' -e 's#/testdata/.*#/x#' -e 's#/[^/]*$##' | sort -u); if [ -n "$p" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$p" | tr '\n' '\0' | xargs -0 go test -timeout 25m -count=1 || r=1; fi; if grep -q '\.test\.js$' "$SDLC_TEST_FILES"; then ./task npm-test || r=1; fi; exit $r; else go test ./... -count=1; fi

_human_gates_doc: pre_commit_pause_paths are the paths the contract holds as risk_tier high, so a
story that touches one waits for a person whatever tier it was written with.
_team_doc: Both lists are lowest first. The project manager chooses each agent's model
and effort from them, story by story; no agent sets 'lowest', so nothing here
bring_back: the paths the contract names as high risk bring security back,
what runs on every tool call brings perf back, and what a person reads
brings the human advocate back, even where the staffing left them out.
